properties.name: A brainstormed idea says it is one, in a property a computation can read
properties.rationale:
Anthony accepted `dec:a-brainstormed-idea-is-a-first-class-kind` 2026-08-30, choosing shape (ii), a declared property rather than a new node type — the latter would make `what_next`, the detectors, the reports, delivery and the merge driver all learn a noun that otherwise behaves exactly like a Decision.

WHY IT WAS BUILT NOW AFTER BEING TWICE JUDGED TOO SMALL: `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` demands a computation read a distinction. A′ — the linking discipline riding the near-match refusal — is that computation, and measured 2026-08-30 it could not be scoped: 207 idea-Decisions and 363 other Decisions differed by nothing readable, `status` does not separate them (32 non-idea Decisions are also `proposed`), and the only remaining signal was the `dec:idea-` ID PREFIX — the defect closed the same morning in #390. Unscoped, A′ would land on the Requirement/Capability/ChangeEvent capture path a consumer's field report names as existing friction, so the marker is what keeps the fix off a live user's path.

⚠️ NO DEFAULT, DELIBERATELY. Absent means NOBODY SAID — a third state, not a synonym for `choice` — following the doctrine `Decision.quality_target` already states. The 207 existing ideas stay UNMARKED: their only evidence of kind is the prefix being retired, so backfilling would launder it into a property. That leaves the existing population unqueryable and is the honest option; whether to backfill anyway is recorded as unsettled.

⚠️ THE SCHEMA STAMP DOES NOT CARRY THIS. It records node and edge type names and counts, and no property names at all, so a consumer pinning a build gains a distinction nothing tells them about. Whether `schema_version` should move for a property addition is unresolved and is now a live question rather than a footnote.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `Decision.kind` declared in schema/structure.yaml — `exploratory` (an idea being turned over, recorded so it is not lost and NOT claimed as intent) or `choice` (a decision somebody faced), indexed, WITH NO DEFAULT. `DecisionReq` gains the field and the tool writes it INSIDE THE SAME CALL rather than through a follow-up setter, because two order-dependent calls is the hazard #392 documented and `cap:a-decision-can-be-created-already-settled` was built to remove for `status`. An undeclared value is refused, and the refusal says omitting is also valid so the obvious repair is not to guess. The brainstorm skill now sets it at capture and both mirrors were re-synced. Four tests, including that ABSENT STAYS ABSENT. Core suite 135 suites / 1548 passed / 0 failed; toolsnaps, schema, skill-lint, doc-versions and self-host gates green.
